Name: Jair, the Gileadite
Summary: Jair, a Gileadite, judged Israel twenty-two years; he had thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts and controlled thirty cities called Havoth-jair. He is distinct from Jair, son of Manasseh, in Numbers.
KeyStory: Jair judged Israel twenty-two years from Gilead, and his thirty sons rode thirty ass colts over thirty cities named Havoth-jair; he died and was buried in Camon.
LifeLesson: Thirty sons and thirty cities — a judge's house looked like a small kingdom.
